subject: mathematics
title: 6.2 Trigonometric Identities — Pythagorean & Reciprocal Proofs
subtitle: Deriving and proving identities with sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ (pp. 242–249)
curiosity_hook: How does Pythagoras' theorem (a² + b² = c²) on a single right triangle generate ALL THREE fundamental trigonometric identities at once?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 Full-Chapter Build (pending human maths teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Derive all three Pythagorean trigonometric identities by dividing Opp² + Adj² = Hyp² by Hyp², Adj², and Opp² respectively.
Distinguish an identity (true for EVERY valid angle θ) from an equation (true only for specific angle values).
Simplify and prove Class 10 trigonometric expressions by converting ratios into sin θ and cos θ or applying difference-of-squares rearrangements.

concept_outline.heading: Pythagoras → The Three Fundamental Identities (p. 242)
concept_outline.summary: Starting from MP² + OM² = OP²: (1) divide by OP² → sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; (2) divide by OM² → 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ (so sec²θ − tan²θ = 1); (3) divide by MP² → 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ (so cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1).

concept_outline.heading: Algebraic Factorisation Trick — sec²θ − tan²θ = 1
concept_outline.summary: Because sec²θ − tan²θ = (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1, (sec θ + tan θ) and (sec θ − tan θ) are exact reciprocals! Likewise (cosec θ + cot θ) and (cosec θ − cot θ) are exact reciprocals.

concept_outline.heading: Reliable Proof Strategy for Exercise 6.1 (pp. 243–249)
concept_outline.summary: Work cleanly from one side (LHS → RHS): convert tan/cot/sec/cosec into sin θ and cos θ, find common denominators, factor using a² − b² or a³ ± b³, and apply sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

key_terms.definition: An equality involving trigonometric ratios that holds true for ALL permissible values of angle θ.
First Pythagorean identity; rearranges to sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ and cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ.
Second Pythagorean identity (for 0° ≤ θ < 90°); yields sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.
Third Pythagorean identity (for 0° < θ ≤ 90°); yields cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

controls.label: Angle θ Identity Verifier
controls.description: Sweep θ across any acute angle to verify numerically that LHS = RHS for all three Pythagorean identities.
controls.keyboard_equivalent: Arrow keys on slider or preset angle buttons.

expected_observations: As θ sweeps from 5° to 85°, individual ratios change rapidly, yet sin²θ + cos²θ stays locked at 1.0000.
1 + tan²θ matches sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ matches cosec²θ identically at every acute angle.
limitations: Numerical verification builds intuition; formal proofs always use algebraic identities rather than plugging one angle.

storyboard.title: Sweep θ and Watch sin²θ + cos²θ
storyboard.learner_action: Test θ = 20°, 45°, and 70° on the triangle workbench.
storyboard.expected_response: All three green identity bars confirm LHS = RHS at every angle.

storyboard.title: Check Boundary Behaviour
storyboard.learner_action: Push θ near 85° and watch tan²θ and sec²θ grow together while their difference remains 1.

accessible_equivalent.summary: Structured KaTeX derivation of the 3 Pythagorean identities and their rearranged reciprocal forms.

steps.heading: Identity 1: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
steps.description: Divide Opp² + Adj² = Hyp² by Hyp². Rearranges to 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ and 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ.

steps.heading: Identity 2: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
steps.description: Divide sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ. Gives (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1.
steps.key_takeaway: sec θ − tan θ = 1 / (sec θ + tan θ).

steps.heading: Identity 3: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ
steps.description: Divide sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by sin²θ. Gives (cosec θ + cot θ)(cosec θ − cot θ) = 1.
steps.key_takeaway: cosec θ − cot θ = 1 / (cosec θ + cot θ).

question_bank.prompt: If sec θ + tan θ = 5, what is the exact value of sec θ − tan θ?
question_bank.hint: Use (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.

options.feedback: Their product equals 1, so they are reciprocals.
Correct! Since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, sec θ − tan θ = 1 / (sec θ + tan θ) = 1/5.
Use difference of squares: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.

question_bank.worked_explanation: (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1 ⇒ 5(sec θ − tan θ) = 1 ⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/5.

question_bank.prompt: Dividing every term of sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by sin²θ (for 0° < θ ≤ 90°) produces which identity?

options.label: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
options.feedback: That comes from dividing by cos²θ.

options.label: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ
options.feedback: Correct! 1 + (cos θ/sin θ)² = (1/sin θ)² ⇒ 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

worked_feedback: Remember the sign rule: sec²θ − tan²θ = +1 (not tan²θ − sec²θ), and cosec²θ − cot²θ = +1.

flashcards.back: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
(sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1 ⇒ they are reciprocals.

flashcards.front: Difference between a Trigonometric Equation and an Identity
flashcards.back: An equation holds only for specific θ values; an identity holds for EVERY valid θ.
